video_title: Carter Bryant PAID for Gilbert Arenas' Sins at Arizona + Got HUMBLED by Vets

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on the unwritten rule to avoid Gilbert Arenas
quotes.excerpt: The first initial thing that anybody that has attended Arizona told me about our alumni is just don't contact Gilbert Arenas.
quotes.quote: The first initial thing that anybody that has attended Arizona told me about our alumni is just don't contact Gilbert Arenas. Like, whatever you do.

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on the physical reality of playing against NBA veterans
quotes.excerpt: The big thing is you're guarding grown men. These dudes are hitting you, you're like, 'Oh yeah, I can tell you have a kid.'
quotes.quote: The big thing is you're guarding grown men. These dudes are hitting you, you're like, 'Oh yeah, I can tell you have a kid.'

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on the humbling experience of his rookie season
quotes.excerpt: I promise you, he probably hit 18 shots in a row, and I'm just like, 'Yo, I should not have put my name in the draft.'
quotes.quote: I promise you, he probably hit 18 shots in a row, and I'm just like, 'Yo, I should not have put my name in the draft. I am not ready to be here.'

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on the physical toll of his first NBA season
quotes.excerpt: After going from playing almost 40 games to playing 82 plus, I think we ended with like 106 games or something like that.
quotes.quote: After going from playing almost 40 games to playing 82 plus, I think we ended with like 106 games or something like that. They were like, 'All right, you've never done this before, so please take two weeks off.' And then it was two weeks straight to playing. So I worked out for like maybe four or five days. That first game was brutal.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the difficult transition from NBA Finals to Summer League
quotes.excerpt: I also went to the finals my rookie year and was guarding Kobe, and then 10 days later they're like, 'You ready for Summer League?'
quotes.quote: I also went to the finals my rookie year and was guarding Kobe, and then 10 days later they're like, 'You ready for Summer League?' I was like, 'What the...?' I'm exhausted.

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on the intensity of NBA defensive schemes
quotes.excerpt: My first 10 games of the season, every time I checked on the court, they just brought me into action and switched in and just tried to run me over.
quotes.quote: My first 10 games of the season, every time I checked on the court, they just brought me into action and switched in and just tried to run me over. I'm like, 'All right, so this is what we're doing. Okay.'

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the reality of proving yourself in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: All they're doing is making you prove who you are. If you prove who you are, then it stops.
quotes.quote: All they're doing is making you prove who you are. If you prove who you are, then it stops. If you don't, it's going to keep getting nasty for you.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on the physical intensity of the 2005 NBA
quotes.excerpt: The rules are so much nicer for you. '05, brother, they were on the other side. They were like Tim Duncan for ice.
quotes.quote: The rules are so much nicer for you. '05, brother, they were on the other side. They were like Tim Duncan for ice. And I go, 'One, two, oh, damn.' And now I'm guarding Tim Duncan trying to do this. He's like, 'That's stop. Give me the ball.' And everyone is on the other side of the court.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Carter Bryant's commitment to his role
quotes.excerpt: Your commitment to what they asked you to be is very clear. There are two or three other spots or teams that you can buy into their commitment to who you're supposed to be for this league for years.
quotes.quote: Your commitment to what they asked you to be is very clear. There are two or three other spots or teams that you can buy into their commitment to who you're supposed to be for this league for years. And when you came up and you were guarding guys full court in Summer League two, three games last year, you could tell somebody said, 'That's how you're going to play.' Was that true, and are you excited about how they built guys like Kawhi, guys like Shaun Livingston?

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on his basketball influences and development
quotes.excerpt: My uncle was a Tim Duncan guy growing up, so I always watched Spurs games. My dad coached Kawhi in high school.
quotes.quote: My uncle was a Tim Duncan guy growing up, so I always watched Spurs games. My dad coached Kawhi in high school. Obviously, Shaun was an Arizona guy. Seeing guys that they develop, guys that were two-way guys, guys that just kind of stand in the corner and just work their tail off on the defensive end. But I understand that at the end of the day, I do the right things to get to earn me more time on the floor and then you progress into doing more things on the basketball court. Our assistant coach Sean Sweeney, that just got the job in Orlando, he was one of the only reasons I played this year. He taught me the game inside out.

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on the impact of coach Sean Sweeney
quotes.excerpt: He taught me the game inside out, like from pounding the ball with your right hand to making a right-hand layup.
quotes.quote: He taught me the game inside out, like from pounding the ball with your right hand to making a right-hand layup to the complexities of the game. And I'm forever in debt to him because he broke everything down to me so simple because I'm a person that has a million and one things going on in my mind and I want to do everything and I think I understand everything. So he taught me how to, yeah.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the steep learning curve of the NBA
quotes.excerpt: You look like you know a lot of basketball. Then you get to the NBA and you realize how much basketball you have no fucking clue about.
quotes.quote: You look like you know a lot of basketball. Then you get to the NBA and you realize how much basketball you have no fucking clue about.

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on his college experience and growth
quotes.excerpt: I think I averaged like five points a game in college. That's like Channing's career numbers.
quotes.quote: I think I averaged like five points a game in college. That's like Channing's career numbers. I was a bucket at Arizona, just FYI.

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on his first experience with Devin Vassell
quotes.excerpt: I walk over there and it's Devin Vassell working out with our coach Jimmy Baron.
quotes.quote: I walk over there and it's Devin Vassell working out with our coach Jimmy Baron. And Jimmy's like, 'Oh, Carter, come over here, guard Devin.' When I tell you, I've never seen a human being hit that many contested shots in a row. Like, I'm playing amazing defense. I'm like, 'Okay, I assume he's going to bust my ass today.' But like, understanding that I've never done this before, so just going and play hard, I promise you, he probably hit 18 shots in a row.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Michael Dickerson's impact on his development
quotes.excerpt: My freshman year, Michael Dickerson, Arizona legend, he cooked me so bad. He cooked me so bad.
quotes.quote: My freshman year, Michael Dickerson, Arizona legend, he cooked me so bad. He cooked me so bad. And I was like, 'If I have to be that good to be the 14th pick in the draft, I'm never going to make it.' And then I went to class the next day.

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on the high level of play in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I did not know Kelly Olynyk was that good. Kelly, yes. Like, I knew Kelly was very good.
quotes.quote: I did not know Kelly Olynyk was that good. Kelly, yes. Like, I knew Kelly was very good. Like, he had the games where he like put teams away and stuff like that, like especially in Boston and then Toronto and like Utah, all those things. Like, he's a hell of a player. When I tell you, he caught it in the post and I had no idea what was going on and he's shooting a one-leg step-back and he pump-fakes and then shoots it off the glass. I'm like, 'He's having fun with you.'

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Kelly Olynyk's skill level
quotes.excerpt: Everything, like Kelly Olynyk was like a second-team All-American. Kelly Olynyk was a second-team All-American.
quotes.quote: Everything, like Kelly Olynyk was like a second-team All-American. Kelly Olynyk was a second-team All-American. And now he's like a nine-year pro. Oh, he's going to cook you. He's good.

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on coach Gregg Popovich
quotes.excerpt: Coach Pop, crazy. Yes, Coach Pop is crazy. I love it because he's a maniac.
quotes.quote: Coach Pop, crazy. Yes, Coach Pop is crazy. I love it because he's a maniac. It's so much fun because myself, my dad coached, my uncle coached in the league a little bit. So I was always around basketball and I with my family's a ton of athletes. My mom and my uncle and my aunt all played volleyball and all types of stuff. So just being around the game and understanding it, like I would sit there with Coach Pop for like an hour and a half after practice and we would just talk about the most random things.

quotes.speaker: Carter Bryant
quotes.summary_phrase: Carter Bryant on his conversations with Gregg Popovich
quotes.excerpt: I remember there was like that stretch where I think it was I missed like 12 dunks in a row.
quotes.quote: I remember there was like that stretch where I think it was I missed like 12 dunks in a row. Like I couldn't get anything to go down. Like he was just telling me stories about stuff like with Kawhi or when he was coaching Bruce Bowen or he's coaching certain guys that ended up being hell of a player. And he's like, 'Yo, this is going to take time. Like, just stay ready. Like, you're going to be a good player.' And when you hear somebody like that telling you, you're going to be a great player and you're going to play in this league for a long time, you're like, 'Oh, okay. Like, just relax a little bit.'

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Gregg Popovich's direct coaching style
quotes.excerpt: He's the type of guy to face -- like not face down, but call me after a game.
quotes.quote: He's the type of guy to face -- like not face down, but call me after a game. I look at him like, Mitch is talking after the game and it's like you know your phone's in the locker room and you just hear some buzzing. I'm like, after I'm like, check, I'm like, 'Oh, this is Coach Pop.' And then he like hits me right after the game. He texts me after every game. So like, but he's he's wild. He's wild. He does like, I remember I was working out one time, he was like, 'You have the worst jab step I've ever seen in my life.' And I was like, 'Oh, okay.' He was like, 'Yeah, you need to immediately go watch Brandon Roy and Kobe and...' He was like, 'You need to go watch those guys and look how they jab, how aggressive it is.' And just little stuff like that. And he's just, I just appreciate how honest he is.
